errors.why: The Tibetan simply says 'this is' and the name of the disease follows on the next side; 'untranscribed text' is a processing artifact, not content.

note: A faithful, clear rendering of the description of the urinary (zagu) disorders, marred only by a stray artifact at the side break.
Accurate rendering of the commentary on who will have faith in the profound Perfection of Wisdom; root-text lemmata and commentary are correctly distinguished.

errors.english: a Bodhisattva [note: an awakened being who vows to liberate all others] who practices according to worldly conduct remains close to complete discipline while engaging in those practices
errors.why: The subject that 'is present' (upasthita) is the Perfection of Wisdom, which stands by to discipline the bodhisattva who practises worldly conduct and to keep him from conceit; the English makes the bodhisattva the one who 'remains close'.

note: The list of benefits is well rendered; the closing gloss on discipline and freedom from pride shifts the subject from the Perfection of Wisdom to the bodhisattva.

errors.english: the status of something as a cause is observed through direct perception
errors.why: The Tibetan says that the causality of the posited quality for cloth etc., apart from their well-known causes, is NOT ascertained either by perception and non-perception or (as with the eye) from the cessation of the effect; the English presents the causality as observed and drops 'apart from the well-known causes'.

note: Generally sound rendering of the refutation of Vaiśeṣika qualities (adṛṣṭa, dharma/adharma, sound), but the opening argument is muddled so the point that the cause is not established is blurred.

errors.english: The suns of the immeasurable Vajra
errors.why: The dual 'dag' names a pair, Amitābha (dpag med) and Vajrasūrya, matching the preceding identification of moon and sun with Amitābha and Ratnasambhava, not 'suns of the immeasurable vajra'.

note: A faithful rendering of the inner moon/sun, channel and wind correlations; only the quoted verse is misconstrued.
Faithful rendering of the distinction between light and light rays and the samādhi miracles; terminology is sound.

errors.english: precious flasks filled with the water of faith
errors.why: ye shes kyi chu is the water of gnosis/wisdom (jñāna), not of faith.

errors.english: the highly praised white, red, and black syllables (Om), (Ah), and (Hum)
errors.why: rab bsngags renders praṇava, i.e. the syllable OṂ itself, not an adjective 'highly praised' qualifying all three syllables.

note: The sādhana sequence (blessing of body, speech, mind, summoning and absorbing the jñānamaṇḍala) is correctly followed, with two terminological slips.

errors.english: Born from karma [note: the original implies action or cause], it is the growth of the head, which is the hair.
errors.why: ལས here is the ablative completing མགོ from the previous side: 'because it grows from the head it is head-born (śiroruha), i.e. hair', not 'born from karma'.

fix.find: Born from karma [note: the original implies action or cause], it is the growth of the head, which is the hair.
fix.replace: Because it grows from the head, it is "head-born," that is, the hair.

note: Careful rendering of the glossed epithets of the wrathful deity and their tantra sources, apart from a misread opening at the side boundary.
Faithful rendering of the Hevajra commentary on bondage and liberation through things, with root-text lemmata and the Laṅkāvatāra quotation correctly handled.

errors.english: [note: referring to the goddess or the specific mantra text Mahapratisara]
errors.why: gsang sngags rjes su 'dzin ma is Mahāmantrānudhāriṇī, a distinct goddess/dhāraṇī of the Pañcarakṣā, not Mahāpratisarā (so sor 'brang ma).

note: A sound rendering of the apotropaic rites and their benefits; only the translator's identification of the vidyārājñī is wrong.
